definitions.explanation: A management philosophy that evaluates and rewards employees based on their output and achievements rather than seniority or hours worked.

examples.japanese: うちの{会社|かいしゃ}は{成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}だ。
examples.english: Our company follows a performance-based system.

examples.japanese: {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}を{導入|どうにゅう}する{企業|きぎょう}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More and more companies are introducing performance-based systems.

examples.japanese: {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}には{賛否|さんぴ}{両論|りょうろん}があり、{社員|しゃいん}のストレスが{増|ふ}えるという{批判|ひはん}もある。
examples.english: There are arguments for and against meritocracy, including criticism that it increases employee stress.

notes:
USAGE:
A buzzword in Japanese business since the late 1990s, when companies began moving away from the traditional {年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ} (seniority-based) system. Still debated in management circles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}を{導入|どうにゅう}する (to introduce a performance-based system)
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}{型|がた}の{評価|ひょうか} (performance-based evaluation)
- {成果|せいか}{主義|しゅぎ}の{弊害|へいがい} (drawbacks of meritocracy)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {年功序列|ねんこうじょれつ}: seniority system — the traditional Japanese model where pay and rank increase with years of service
- {実力主義|じつりょくしゅぎ}: meritocracy based on ability — similar but emphasizes skill rather than measurable output
